## formal
Let $k$ be $\Q$ or a subfield of $\R$, and $\Cl_{k}(2,2)$ the algebra of two modes of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.chsh-bound-for-two-subsystems-of-a-clifford-algebra-by-a-rational-certificate}, clause (vii): generators $e_{j}$, $f_{j}$ with $Q(e_{j}) = 1$, $Q(f_{j}) = -1$, $p_{j} = f_{j}e_{j}$, the adjoint $\dagger$ the linear extension of the inverse on blades, $\langle x\rangle_{0}$ the scalar part. Write
\[
X_{1} = e_{1}, \quad Z_{1} = p_{1}, \quad X_{2} = e_{2}p_{1}, \quad Z_{2} = p_{2}, \qquad U = X_{1}X_{2}, \quad V = Z_{1}Z_{2}, \quad K = e_{1}f_{2} .
\]
$X_{2}$ is the twisted generator of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}. A \emph{direction} of party $1$ is $a = xX_{1} + zZ_{1}$ and of party $2$ is $b = x'X_{2} + z'Z_{2}$, with $x, z, x', z' \in k$, $x^{2} + z^{2} = x'^{2} + z'^{2} = 1$; directions are self-adjoint of square $1$, and those of party $1$ commute with those of party $2$. For directions $a_{1}, a_{2}, b_{1}, b_{2}$ let $C = a_{1}(b_{1} + b_{2}) + a_{2}(b_{1} - b_{2})$. The \emph{local products} are the elements of the span $L$ of the nine products $st$, $s \in \{1, X_{1}, Z_{1}\}$, $t \in \{1, X_{2}, Z_{2}\}$: products of local observables (self-adjoint elements of the two parties), not of arbitrary local elements. $L$ contains every direction, every product $ab$ and every $C$. It is not the whole algebra: the algebras of the two parties together span $\Cl_{k}(2,2)$, and $K = -(X_{1}Z_{1})(X_{2}Z_{2}) = -f_{1}\cdot f_{2}p_{1}$ is a product of one anti-self-adjoint element of each party's algebra that does not lie in $L$. The \emph{weight} of the outcomes $(+,+)$ of a pair of directions is the value of $\tfrac14(1 + a)(1 + b)$; the other outcomes are the pairs $(\pm a, \pm b)$.

\emph{Hypothesis (L), non-negative local weights:} $\lambda : \Cl_{k}(2,2) \to k$ is $k$-linear with $\lambda(1) = 1$ and $\lambda\bigl(\tfrac14(1 + a)(1 + b)\bigr) \ge 0$ for every direction $a$ of party $1$ and $b$ of party $2$. (P) is Premise \claimref{synthesis.premise-positivity-of-values}. Neither is assumed here: the clauses compare them.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{((P) gives (L); proved.)} $\tfrac14(1 + a)(1 + b)$ is a self-adjoint idempotent $y = yy^{\dagger}$, so a functional satisfying (P) satisfies (L).
\item[(ii)] \emph{((L) gives the CHSH bound; proved.)} Under (L), $|\lambda(ab)| \le 1$ for all directions and $\lambda(C)^{2} \le 8$ for every $C$ built from directions; for $k = \Q$ the inequality is strict. No positivity on any other element is used, and not the reality clause.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The box functional fails (L); proved.)} The functional $\lambda_{\mathrm{box}}(x) = \langle(1 + C_{0})x\rangle_{0}$, $C_{0}$ the element $C$ at $a_{1} = X_{1}$, $a_{2} = Z_{1}$, $b_{1} = X_{2}$, $b_{2} = Z_{2}$ (the functional of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.chsh-bound-needs-positivity-across-settings-and-anticommutation-holds-only-on-the-state}, with value $4$ on $C_{0}$ and non-negative weights at its four pairs of settings), has $\lambda_{\mathrm{box}}(X_{1}b) = \tfrac75$ and the weight $\lambda_{\mathrm{box}}\bigl(\tfrac14(1 + X_{1})(1 - b)\bigr) = -\tfrac{1}{10}$ at the direction $b = \tfrac35X_{2} + \tfrac45Z_{2}$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{((L) and the values of all local products do not give (P); proved.)} $U$, $V$, $K$ are self-adjoint blades of square $1$, $UV = VU = -K$, and $K \notin L$. For $c \in k$ let $\lambda_{c}(x) = \langle(1 - U - V + cK)x\rangle_{0}$. Every $\lambda_{c}$ is linear with $\lambda_{c}(1) = 1$, $\lambda_{c}(x^{\dagger}) = \lambda_{c}(x)$, is even ($\lambda_{c}$ vanishes on odd elements), satisfies (L), and has on $L$ the values that do not depend on $c$: $\lambda_{c}(ab) = -(xx' + zz')$, $\lambda_{c}(a) = \lambda_{c}(b) = 0$, so every weight at a pair of directions is $\tfrac14(1 - xx' - zz')$ and every value $\lambda_{c}(C)$ is the same for all $c$. $\lambda_{c}(K) = c$. $\lambda_{c}$ satisfies (P) if and only if $c = -1$; $\lambda_{-1}(x) = 4\langle P_{s}x\rangle_{0}$ with $P_{s} = \tfrac14(1 - U)(1 - V)$ a self-adjoint idempotent with $P_{s}xP_{s} = 4\langle P_{s}x\rangle_{0}P_{s}$ for all $x$. For $c \ne -1$ a negative value occurs on a joint outcome of the commuting pair $U$, $V$: $\lambda_{c}\bigl(\tfrac14(1 + uU)(1 + vV)\bigr) = \tfrac14(1 - u - v - c\,uv)$ for $u, v = \pm 1$, which is $-\tfrac14(1 + c)$ at $(+,+)$ and $\tfrac14(1 + c)$ at $(+,-)$. So two functionals that agree on every local product, on every weight of a pair of directions and on every CHSH value of directions differ on (P); what separates them is the value of the one blade $K$, equivalently the weights of the joint outcomes of $U$ and $V$, a pair of commuting observables each of which is a product of local directions and whose joint outcome idempotents are not local products.
\item[(v)] \emph{(The two descents; proved.)} Let $E_{N}(x) = \tfrac14\sum_{g}gxg$, $g \in \{1, p_{1}, p_{2}, p_{1}p_{2}\}$, the composite of the mode-wise parity averages (Proposition \claimref{singularity.p-reduced-metric-level-reading-many}), and $E(x) = \tfrac12(x + \Gamma x\Gamma)$, $\Gamma = p_{1}p_{2}$, the total-parity average (Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average} in its total-parity form). With $\Pi_{n} = \tfrac14(1 + n_{1}p_{1})(1 + n_{2}p_{2})$, $n_{1}, n_{2} = \pm 1$: $E_{N}(x) = \sum_{n}\Pi_{n}x\Pi_{n} = 4\sum_{n}\langle\Pi_{n}x\rangle_{0}\Pi_{n}$, so for every linear $\lambda$ with $\lambda(1) = 1$ the functional $\lambda \circ E_{N}$ is $x \mapsto 4\sum_{n}\lambda(\Pi_{n})\langle\Pi_{n}x\rangle_{0}$, and it satisfies (P) if and only if the four numbers $\lambda(\Pi_{n})$ are non-negative. $\lambda_{c} \circ E_{N}$ for every $c$ and $\lambda_{\mathrm{box}} \circ E_{N}$ are all the functional $\langle(1 - V)x\rangle_{0}$, which satisfies (P). For the total-parity average, $\lambda_{c} \circ E = \lambda_{c}$ for every $c$, and $\lambda_{\mathrm{box}} \circ E = \langle(1 + U - V)x\rangle_{0}$ has the value $-\tfrac14$ on the self-adjoint idempotent $\tfrac14(1 - U)(1 + V)$: the total-parity average of a functional that violates (P) can violate (P).
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} (P) implies (L), (L) implies the CHSH bound for directions, and neither implication reverses: the box functional satisfies neither, and $\lambda_{c}$, $c \ne -1$, satisfies (L) and not (P). In this realisation the bound therefore does not need positivity on elements that combine settings; it needs non-negative weights at every pair of local directions, not only at the four pairs of a configuration. What (P) adds to (L) is not visible in the values of local products, on this algebra: this is the failure of local tomography for an algebra over the reals whose adjoint is a transpose, a classical fact, here in its exact form (the one blade $K$). The statement corrects, for this realisation only, a sentence of Premise \claimref{synthesis.premise-positivity-of-values} (formal level, paragraph on what it costs): ``Positivity is asked on every element $xx^{\dagger}$, including those that combine quantities which the two parties never measure together; that is the part the counter-model shows cannot be dropped, and it is assumed.'' The counter-model shows that non-negative weights at its four pairs of settings do not give the bound; by (ii) and (iii), with one twisted mode per party the part that cannot be dropped for the bound is non-negativity of the weights at pairs of local directions outside those four, each of which the two parties can measure together. The general statement on the mode-wise and the total-parity average, for any number of modes, is in the sibling result on weights on effects of the same run (intended citation, not yet stored); clause (v) keeps the two-mode instances. A premise that is a statement about recorded outcomes of local directions cannot distinguish $\lambda_{-1}$ from $\lambda_{c}$; that the stored premises on recording, on superselection of recorded sectors and on supervenience are of that kind is argued, not proved. Of the two stored readings of the descent on several modes, the mode-wise one reduces (P) to the non-negativity of the weights of the number sectors, and the total-parity one leaves (P) a separate condition.

## technical
Premise (P), positivity of values, asks that values be given by a linear functional that is non-negative on every $xx^{\dagger}$. For two parties, each with the directions of one mode of $\Cl_{k}(2,2)$, for $k$ a subfield of the reals (the second mode twisted so that the parties commute), a weaker condition (L) asks only that the weights of the joint outcomes of every pair of local directions be non-negative. Three things are proved. First, (L) already gives the CHSH bound: the correlation of two directions is a bilinear form of their coordinates bounded by $1$ on unit vectors, which gives a squared CHSH value of at most $8$. The box functional of value $4$ has non-negative weights at its own four pairs of settings and a weight $-1/10$ at another rational pair, so it is excluded by (L) without (P). Second, (L) does not give (P): the functionals $\langle(1 - U - V + cK)x\rangle_{0}$, one for each number $c$, agree on every product of local directions, so on every local weight and every CHSH value, and only the one with $c = -1$ satisfies (P); the others give a negative weight to a joint outcome of the commuting products $U = X_{1}X_{2}$ and $V = Z_{1}Z_{2}$. The values of local products leave the value of the blade $K = e_{1}f_{2}$ free, and (P) fixes it. Third, the mode-wise parity average sends every one of these functionals, and the box, to the same functional, which satisfies (P) because after that average (P) is the non-negativity of the four weights of the number sectors; the total-parity average leaves the family unchanged and leaves the box functional in violation of (P). So, on this algebra, (P) is independent of the values of all products of local observables (the known failure of local tomography over the reals) and is not produced by the total-parity descent; under the mode-wise descent it is the non-negativity of ordinary weights.

## lay
The series assumes that averages of measured quantities come from a rule that never gives a negative average to a quantity multiplied by its mirror image; this is assumption (P). One reason given for it was that without it two distant experimenters could be more strongly correlated than quantum theory allows. This result looks at what is really needed. If one only asks that every probability the two experimenters can obtain, for every choice of what each measures, is not negative, the quantum limit already follows, in the simplest setting of one mode each. The well-known rule that reaches the largest correlation fails this weaker request: it gives a negative probability for a choice of measurements it was not designed for. But the weaker request is not the same as (P). There is a family of rules that give exactly the same probabilities for everything the two experimenters can measure separately, and only one member of the family obeys (P); the others give a negative probability only for a joint measurement that neither experimenter can make alone. So, in this setting of one mode each, (P) cannot be read off from separate measurements; this is a known feature of quantum theory over the real numbers. The series' procedure of averaging over the parity of each mode makes all these rules equal and harmless; averaging only over the total parity does not.

## one-liner
In $\Cl_{k}(2,2)$, $k$ a subfield of $\R$, with one twisted mode per party and directions as observables, non-negative weights at every pair of local directions give $\lambda(C)^{2} \le 8$ without (P) and exclude the box functional (weight $-\tfrac{1}{10}$); the functionals $\langle(1 - U - V + cK)x\rangle_{0}$ agree on all products of local observables and satisfy (P) only for $c = -1$; the mode-wise parity average reduces (P) to four non-negative weights, the total-parity average does not give it.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{Preliminaries.} The adjoint, the scalar part and their properties ($\langle x^{\dagger}\rangle_{0} = \langle x\rangle_{0}$, $\langle xy\rangle_{0} = \langle yx\rangle_{0}$, $\langle x^{\dagger}x\rangle_{0}$ the sum of the squares of the coefficients of $x$, the scalar part of a product of two blades zero unless they are equal up to sign) are those of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.chsh-bound-for-two-subsystems-of-a-clifford-algebra-by-a-rational-certificate}; the blades are a basis by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}. By clause (vii) of the former and Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, $X_{1}, Z_{1}, X_{2}, Z_{2}$ are self-adjoint blades of square $1$, $X_{1}Z_{1} = -Z_{1}X_{1}$, $X_{2}Z_{2} = -Z_{2}X_{2}$, and each of $X_{1}, Z_{1}$ commutes with each of $X_{2}, Z_{2}$. Hence a direction has square $x^{2} + z^{2} = 1$ and is self-adjoint, and directions of different parties commute. $U = X_{1}X_{2}$ and $V = Z_{1}Z_{2}$ are products of commuting self-adjoint elements of square $1$, so they are self-adjoint of square $1$; $UV = X_{1}X_{2}Z_{1}Z_{2} = X_{1}Z_{1}X_{2}Z_{2} = VU$ (two anticommutations), and $X_{1}Z_{1} = e_{1}f_{1}e_{1} = -f_{1}$, $X_{2}Z_{2} = e_{2}p_{1}f_{2}e_{2} = -f_{2}p_{1}$, so $UV = f_{1}f_{2}p_{1} = f_{1}f_{2}f_{1}e_{1} = f_{2}e_{1} = -K$ with $K = e_{1}f_{2}$, a blade with $K^{\dagger} = f_{2}^{\dagger}e_{1}^{\dagger} = -f_{2}e_{1} = K$ and $K^{2} = 1$. The nine products spanning $L$ are, up to sign, the nine distinct blades $1, e_{1}, p_{1}, e_{2}p_{1}, p_{2}, e_{1}e_{2}p_{1}, e_{1}p_{2}, p_{1}e_{2}p_{1} = e_{2}, p_{1}p_{2}$, none of them $\pm e_{1}f_{2}$; so $K \notin L$, while $K = -(X_{1}Z_{1})(X_{2}Z_{2})$ with $X_{1}Z_{1} = -f_{1}$ and $X_{2}Z_{2} = -f_{2}p_{1}$ anti-self-adjoint (verified by the check), and $\langle Ky\rangle_{0} = 0$ for $y \in L$.

\emph{(i).} $y = \tfrac14(1 + a)(1 + b)$ is a product of two commuting self-adjoint idempotents, so $y^{\dagger} = y = y^{2} = yy^{\dagger}$, and (P) gives $\lambda(y) \ge 0$.

\emph{(ii).} If $a$, $b$ are directions so are $-a$, $-b$. As elements, $\tfrac14(1 + a)(1 + b) + \tfrac14(1 - a)(1 - b) = \tfrac12(1 + ab)$ and $\tfrac14(1 + a)(1 - b) + \tfrac14(1 - a)(1 + b) = \tfrac12(1 - ab)$. Under (L) the left sides have non-negative values, so $1 + \lambda(ab) \ge 0$ and $1 - \lambda(ab) \ge 0$: $|\lambda(ab)| \le 1$. The map $\beta(a, b) = \lambda(ab)$, extended linearly to the plane spanned by $X_{1}, Z_{1}$ and the plane spanned by $X_{2}, Z_{2}$, is a bilinear form on these two planes with values in $k \subseteq \R$, fixed by its four values on the generators; write $|a|^{2} = x^{2} + z^{2}$ for $a = xX_{1} + zZ_{1}$, which is $a^{2}$, and likewise for $b$. So $|\beta(a, b)| \le 1$ for all $a$, $b$ of norm one with coordinates in $k$. The points of norm one with coordinates in $\Q$, hence in $k$, are dense in those with real coordinates (the points $((1 - s^{2})/(1 + s^{2}), 2s/(1 + s^{2}))$, $s \in \Q$), and $\beta$, extended to real coordinates, is continuous, so $|\beta(a, b)| \le 1$ at norm one and $|\beta(a, b)| \le |a|\,|b|$ for all elements of the two real planes. For directions $a_{1}, a_{2}, b_{1}, b_{2}$,
\[
\lambda(C) = \beta(a_{1}, b_{1} + b_{2}) + \beta(a_{2}, b_{1} - b_{2}), \qquad |\lambda(C)| \le |b_{1} + b_{2}| + |b_{1} - b_{2}| ,
\]
and $|b_{1} + b_{2}|^{2} + |b_{1} - b_{2}|^{2} = 2|b_{1}|^{2} + 2|b_{2}|^{2} = 4$, so $\lambda(C)^{2} \le 2 \cdot 4 = 8$ by $(s + d)^{2} \le 2(s^{2} + d^{2})$. For $k = \Q$ the value $\lambda(C)$ is rational and $8$ is not the square of a rational, so the inequality is strict. Only the weights at pairs of directions were used.

\emph{(iii).} $C_{0} = X_{1}X_{2} + X_{1}Z_{2} + Z_{1}X_{2} - Z_{1}Z_{2}$ is a sum of four distinct blades up to sign, none scalar, so $\lambda_{\mathrm{box}}(1) = 1$, $\lambda_{\mathrm{box}}(C_{0}) = \langle C_{0}^{2}\rangle_{0} = 4$, the values on the four products are $1, 1, 1, -1$, and the values on $X_{1}, Z_{1}, X_{2}, Z_{2}$ are $0$; this is the functional of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.chsh-bound-needs-positivity-across-settings-and-anticommutation-holds-only-on-the-state} with the settings named in another order. For $b = \tfrac35X_{2} + \tfrac45Z_{2}$: $\lambda_{\mathrm{box}}(X_{1}b) = \tfrac35 + \tfrac45 = \tfrac75$ and $\lambda_{\mathrm{box}}\bigl(\tfrac14(1 + X_{1})(1 - b)\bigr) = \tfrac14(1 - \tfrac75) = -\tfrac{1}{10}$.

\emph{(iv).} $M_{c} = 1 - U - V + cK$ is self-adjoint and even, with scalar part $1$, so $\lambda_{c}(1) = 1$, $\lambda_{c}(x^{\dagger}) = \langle M_{c}x^{\dagger}\rangle_{0} = \langle xM_{c}\rangle_{0} = \lambda_{c}(x)$, and $\lambda_{c}$ vanishes on odd $x$ (the product $M_{c}x$ is then odd). On $L$ the term $cK$ contributes nothing, by the preliminaries; the other terms give $\lambda_{c}(X_{1}X_{2}) = \lambda_{c}(Z_{1}Z_{2}) = -1$ and $0$ on the other seven products, whence $\lambda_{c}(ab) = -(xx' + zz')$, $\lambda_{c}(a) = \lambda_{c}(b) = 0$ and the weight $\tfrac14(1 - xx' - zz') \ge 0$ (Cauchy's inequality for two unit vectors): (L) holds for every $c$. $\lambda_{c}(K) = c\langle K^{2}\rangle_{0} = c$. Since $U$, $V$ commute, have square $1$ and $UV = -K$, the four elements $\tfrac14(1 + uU)(1 + vV)$ are self-adjoint idempotents and $M_{c}\,\tfrac14(1 + uU)(1 + vV) = (1 - u - v - c\,uv)\,\tfrac14(1 + uU)(1 + vV)$; each has scalar part $\tfrac14$ ($U$, $V$, $UV$ are non-scalar blades), which gives the table. If $c \ne -1$ one of $\mp\tfrac14(1 + c)$ is negative on an element $yy^{\dagger}$, so (P) fails. If $c = -1$, $M_{-1} = (1 - U)(1 - V) = 4P_{s}$ and $\lambda_{-1}(xx^{\dagger}) = 4\langle P_{s}xx^{\dagger}P_{s}\rangle_{0} = 4\langle(P_{s}x)(P_{s}x)^{\dagger}\rangle_{0} \ge 0$, so (P) holds. The identity $P_{s}xP_{s} = 4\langle P_{s}x\rangle_{0}P_{s}$ is linear in $x$ and is verified on the sixteen blades by the check. The check also evaluates every statement of this clause for five values of $c$; each is affine in $c$.

\emph{(v).} The average over conjugation by one mode parity is the descent of Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average} for that mode, and the composite of the mode-wise averages is the map $E_{N}$ of Proposition \claimref{singularity.p-reduced-metric-level-reading-many}; the same theorem with $\Gamma$ in place of the mode parity is the total-parity average $E$. Conjugation by $p_{j}$ multiplies a blade by $\pm 1$, so $E_{N}$ is the projection onto the span of the blades fixed by both conjugations, which are $1, p_{1}, p_{2}, p_{1}p_{2}$; this span is also the span of the four $\Pi_{n}$, which are orthogonal self-adjoint idempotents with sum $1$ and scalar part $\tfrac14$, commuting with $p_{1}$, $p_{2}$. Expanding $\sum_{n}\Pi_{n}x\Pi_{n}$ in the group elements gives $\tfrac14\sum_{g}gxg$; and $\Pi_{n}x\Pi_{n}$ lies in the fixed span and equals $\Pi_{n}(\cdot)\Pi_{n}$ of it, so it is a multiple of $\Pi_{n}$, the multiple being $4\langle\Pi_{n}x\rangle_{0}$ by taking scalar parts. Both formulas are verified on all blades. Hence $\lambda(E_{N}(x)) = 4\sum_{n}\lambda(\Pi_{n})\langle\Pi_{n}x\rangle_{0}$. If all $\lambda(\Pi_{n}) \ge 0$ this is non-negative on $xx^{\dagger}$ as in (iv), is normalised, and is real because each $\Pi_{n}$ is self-adjoint; conversely $\lambda(E_{N}(\Pi_{n}\Pi_{n}^{\dagger})) = \lambda(\Pi_{n})$. For $M_{c}$ and $1 + C_{0}$ the fixed part is $1 - V$ ($V = p_{1}p_{2}$; $U$, $K$ and the other blades of $C_{0}$ are not fixed), with weights $0, \tfrac12, \tfrac12, 0$, and $1 - V = \tfrac12(1 - V)^{2}$. For the total parity, conjugation by $\Gamma$ fixes even blades and negates odd ones, so $M_{c}$ is fixed and the even part of $1 + C_{0}$ is $1 + U - V$; with $y = \tfrac14(1 - U)(1 + V) = yy^{\dagger}$, $(1 + U - V)y = -y$ and the value is $-\langle y\rangle_{0} = -\tfrac14$.

"""synthesis.local-weights-give-the-chsh-bound-and-do-not-fix-positivity-of-values: exact checks.

Cl(2,2) of two modes: e_k (square +1, index 2k), f_k (square -1, index 2k+1), p_k = f_k e_k; the dagger sends a
blade to its inverse. X1 = e_1, Z1 = p_1, X2 = e_2 p_1, Z2 = p_2; U = X1 X2, V = Z1 Z2, K = e_1 f_2 = -U V.
Functionals lam_c(x) = <(1 - U - V + c K) x>_0 and the box <(1 + C) x>_0.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import combinations, product

import GA
from tp_premise import premise

ONE = GA.sc(F(1))


def dsign(b, sq):
    g = len(b)
    s = (-1) ** (g * (g - 1) // 2)
    for i in b:
        s *= sq[i]
    return s


def dagger(x, sq):
    return {b: c * dsign(b, sq) for b, c in x.items()}


def clean(x):
    return {b: c for b, c in x.items() if c != 0}


def prod(sq, *xs):
    r = ONE
    for x in xs:
        r = GA.mul(r, x, sq)
    return clean(r)


def lin(*terms):
    r = {}
    for c, x in terms:
        r = GA.add(r, GA.scal(F(c), x))
    return clean(r)


def s0(x):
    return x.get((), F(0))


def par(x):
    return {b: (c if len(b) % 2 == 0 else -c) for b, c in x.items()}


def setup():
    sq = (1, -1, 1, -1)
    e = [GA.gen(0), GA.gen(2)]
    f = [GA.gen(1), GA.gen(3)]
    p = [prod(sq, f[k], e[k]) for k in range(2)]
    x1, z1, x2, z2 = e[0], p[0], prod(sq, e[1], p[0]), p[1]
    u, v, k = prod(sq, x1, x2), prod(sq, z1, z2), prod(sq, e[0], f[1])
    blades = [ONE] + [{tuple(c): F(1)} for r in range(1, 5) for c in combinations(range(4), r)]
    return sq, p, x1, z1, x2, z2, u, v, k, blades


def chsh(sq, a1, a2, b1, b2):
    return lin((1, prod(sq, a1, b1)), (1, prod(sq, a1, b2)), (1, prod(sq, a2, b1)), (-1, prod(sq, a2, b2)))


def unit(s):
    """Rational point of the unit circle with parameter s."""
    s = F(s)
    return ((1 - s * s) / (1 + s * s), 2 * s / (1 + s * s))


PARAMS = [F(0), F(1), F(-1), F(1, 2), F(-1, 2), F(2), F(-3), F(1, 3), F(2, 3), F(-5, 4)]


def is_obs(x, sq):
    return clean(dagger(x, sq)) == clean(x) and prod(sq, x, x) == ONE


def check_local_weights_bound_values_and_the_box_fails_them():
    premise("synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra")
    premise("tower.commuting-copies")
    premise("synthesis.chsh-bound-for-two-subsystems-of-a-clifford-algebra-by-a-rational-certificate")
    premise("synthesis.chsh-bound-needs-positivity-across-settings-and-anticommutation-holds-only-on-the-state")
    sq, p, x1, z1, x2, z2, u, v, k, blades = setup()
    dirs = [unit(s) for s in PARAMS] + [(-c, -d) for c, d in (unit(s) for s in PARAMS)]
    da = [lin((c, x1), (d, z1)) for c, d in dirs]
    db = [lin((c, x2), (d, z2)) for c, d in dirs]
    assert all(is_obs(a, sq) for a in da + db)
    assert all(GA.commutes(a, b, sq) for a in (x1, z1) for b in (x2, z2))
    half = F(1, 2)
    w = lambda a, b: prod(sq, lin((half, ONE), (half, a)), lin((half, ONE), (half, b)))
    # a weight element is y y^dagger with y itself, and the two sums of opposite weights
    for a, b in ((da[3], db[7]), (x1, z2), (da[9], db[2])):
        y = w(a, b)
        assert prod(sq, y, dagger(y, sq)) == y
        na, nb = GA.neg(a), GA.neg(b)
        assert lin((1, w(a, b)), (1, w(na, nb))) == lin((half, ONE), (half, prod(sq, a, b)))
        assert lin((1, w(a, nb)), (1, w(na, b))) == lin((half, ONE), (-half, prod(sq, a, b)))
    # the box: value 4, matrix T with a unit pair of value 7/5, weight -1/10
    c = chsh(sq, x1, z1, x2, z2)
    box = lambda x: s0(prod(sq, lin((1, ONE), (1, c)), x))
    assert box(ONE) == 1 and box(c) == 4
    assert [box(prod(sq, a, b)) for a in (x1, z1) for b in (x2, z2)] == [1, 1, 1, -1]
    bb = lin((F(3, 5), x2), (F(4, 5), z2))
    assert is_obs(bb, sq) and box(prod(sq, x1, bb)) == F(7, 5)
    assert box(w(x1, GA.neg(bb))) == F(-1, 10) and box(w(GA.neg(x1), bb)) == F(-1, 10)
    assert box(w(x1, bb)) == F(6, 10)
    # lam_c: weights (1 - xi.eta)/4 >= 0 and CHSH values of square below 8, the same for every c
    for cc in (F(-1), F(0), F(1), F(3)):
        m = lin((1, ONE), (-1, u), (-1, v), (cc, k))
        lam = lambda x: s0(prod(sq, m, x))
        assert lam(ONE) == 1
        for (i, a), (j, b) in product(enumerate(da), enumerate(db)):
            wt = lam(w(a, b))
            assert wt == (1 - dirs[i][0] * dirs[j][0] - dirs[i][1] * dirs[j][1]) / 4 and wt >= 0
        best = F(0)
        for i1, i2, j1, j2 in product(range(0, 20, 3), repeat=4):
            val = lam(chsh(sq, da[i1], da[i2], db[j1], db[j2]))
            assert val * val < 8
            best = max(best, val)
        assert best == F(14, 5)
    return True


def check_local_values_do_not_fix_positivity():
    premise("synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra")
    premise("tower.commuting-copies")
    sq, p, x1, z1, x2, z2, u, v, k, blades = setup()
    assert is_obs(u, sq) and is_obs(v, sq) and is_obs(k, sq) and GA.commutes(u, v, sq)
    assert prod(sq, u, v) == GA.neg(k)
    y1, y2 = prod(sq, x1, z1), prod(sq, x2, z2)
    assert k == GA.neg(prod(sq, y1, y2)) and y1 == GA.neg(GA.gen(1)) and y2 == GA.neg(prod(sq, GA.gen(3), p[0]))
    assert clean(dagger(y1, sq)) == GA.neg(y1) and clean(dagger(y2, sq)) == GA.neg(y2)
    loc = [prod(sq, a, b) for a in (ONE, x1, z1) for b in (ONE, x2, z2)]
    keys = set()
    for y in loc:
        assert len(y) == 1
        keys.add(next(iter(y)))
    assert len(keys) == 9 and next(iter(k)) not in keys
    ps = lin((F(1, 4), ONE), (F(-1, 4), u), (F(-1, 4), v), (F(1, 4), prod(sq, u, v)))
    assert prod(sq, ps, ps) == ps and clean(dagger(ps, sq)) == ps and s0(ps) == F(1, 4)
    assert all(prod(sq, ps, b, ps) == clean(GA.scal(4 * s0(prod(sq, ps, b)), ps)) for b in blades)
    quarter = F(1, 4)
    tab = lambda lam, su, sv: lam(prod(sq, lin((F(1, 2), ONE), (F(su, 2), u)), lin((F(1, 2), ONE), (F(sv, 2), v))))
    ref = None
    for cc in (F(-1), F(0), F(1), F(3), F(-2)):
        m = lin((1, ONE), (-1, u), (-1, v), (cc, k))
        lam = lambda x: s0(prod(sq, m, x))
        vals = [lam(y) for y in loc]
        ref = vals if ref is None else ref
        assert vals == ref == [1, 0, 0, 0, -1, 0, 0, 0, -1]
        assert all(lam(dagger(b, sq)) == lam(b) and lam(par(b)) == lam(b) for b in blades)
        assert lam(k) == cc and lam(ps) == (3 - cc) / 4
        t = {(su, sv): tab(lam, su, sv) for su in (1, -1) for sv in (1, -1)}
        assert t[(1, 1)] == -(1 + cc) * quarter and t[(1, -1)] == (1 + cc) * quarter
        assert t[(-1, 1)] == (1 + cc) * quarter and t[(-1, -1)] == (3 - cc) * quarter
        assert (min(t.values()) >= 0) == (cc == -1)
        if cc == -1:
            assert m == clean(GA.scal(F(4), ps))
    return True


def check_descents_mode_wise_gives_positivity_total_parity_does_not():
    premise("singularity.descent-parity-average")
    premise("singularity.p-reduced-metric-level-reading-many")
    premise("synthesis.chsh-bound-needs-positivity-across-settings-and-anticommutation-holds-only-on-the-state")
    sq, p, x1, z1, x2, z2, u, v, k, blades = setup()
    gam = prod(sq, p[0], p[1])
    assert gam == v
    grp = [ONE, p[0], p[1], gam]
    pis = [prod(sq, lin((F(1, 2), ONE), (F(n1, 2), p[0])), lin((F(1, 2), ONE), (F(n2, 2), p[1])))
           for n1 in (1, -1) for n2 in (1, -1)]
    en = lambda x: clean(GA.scal(F(1, 4), GA.add(*[prod(sq, g, x, g) for g in grp])))
    for b in blades:
        assert en(b) == lin(*[(4 * s0(prod(sq, q, b)), q) for q in pis])
        assert en(b) == lin(*[(1, prod(sq, q, b, q)) for q in pis])
    c = chsh(sq, x1, z1, x2, z2)
    dens = [lin((1, ONE), (1, c))] + [lin((1, ONE), (-1, u), (-1, v), (cc, k)) for cc in (F(-1), F(0), F(1), F(3))]
    target = lin((1, ONE), (-1, v))
    for m in dens:
        assert en(m) == target
        assert [s0(prod(sq, m, q)) for q in pis] == [0, F(1, 2), F(1, 2), 0]
    assert target == lin((F(1, 2), prod(sq, lin((1, ONE), (-1, v)), lin((1, ONE), (-1, v)))))
    # total parity average: lam_c unchanged; the box becomes <(1 + U - V) x>_0, negative on y y^dagger
    ev = lambda x: clean(GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(x, prod(sq, gam, x, gam))))
    for m in dens[1:]:
        assert ev(m) == m
    mb = ev(dens[0])
    assert mb == lin((1, ONE), (1, u), (-1, v))
    y = prod(sq, lin((F(1, 2), ONE), (F(-1, 2), u)), lin((F(1, 2), ONE), (F(1, 2), v)))
    assert prod(sq, y, dagger(y, sq)) == y and s0(prod(sq, mb, y)) == F(-1, 4)
    return True
